reference_memory.normal_pattern: The time series exhibits a highly regular, quasi-sinusoidal oscillation with a robust period of ~183 points, consistent across all candidates. Each cycle consists of a sharp, near-symmetric rise to a single smooth peak followed by a slower, slightly asymmetric decay to a trough; the rise is steeper than the fall, giving a slight right-skew to each cycle. Peak amplitudes (robust standardized) range from ~3.0 to ~4.1, with troughs consistently near -1.0 to -0.5. Baseline level (median) varies modestly between -0.27 and +0.12 across windows, indicating small drift but no strong trend—slope per point is near zero (±0.0007), well within noise. Roughness (~0.032) and curvature (~0.0138) are stable across multi-cycle segments, confirming morphological consistency. Noise is low: the signal is smooth with minimal high-frequency jitter; local minima/maxima are well-defined and repeatable. The first candidate (1P) shows only one full cycle and appears truncated at both ends, but its internal morphology matches the others. Multi-cycle candidates (3P and 5P) confirm that cycle shape does not degrade over time and that inter-cycle spacing is precise. Acceptable variation includes minor amplitude modulation (±0.5 in peak height), slight baseline shift (<0.4 units), and negligible phase jitter (<5 points). No outliers or abrupt regime changes appear in the consensus.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle segment (1P); shows one complete oscillation with a gentle pre-peak dip, a smooth peak near index 134, and a symmetric-looking descent. Truncated at both ends—starts below baseline and ends near zero—so full trough-to-trough context is missing. Morphology aligns with later cycles but lacks repetition confirmation.

Three full cycles (3P); clear repetition of sharp rises, rounded peaks (~4.0), and gradual decays. Troughs consistently near -1.0. Minor baseline drift visible (slight downward slope), but cycle shape is identical across repetitions. High fidelity to expected periodicity.

Another three-cycle segment (3P); nearly identical to reference 1 in morphology, amplitude, and timing. Slight upward baseline drift compensates for prior downward trend, reinforcing that baseline shifts are slow and reversible. Peak heights marginally lower (~3.8 vs 4.0), within normal amplitude variation.

Five-cycle segment (5P); confirms long-term stability. All five cycles preserve the same rise/decay asymmetry, peak width, and trough depth. Final cycle ends abruptly (truncation at right edge), but prior four are fully intact. Amplitude slightly higher on average (~4.4), still within 90th-percentile envelope.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 1 or 2 for query windows of ~3 cycles due to highest reliability and clean morphology; use reference 3 when analyzing longer windows (>4 cycles) to capture extended stability; use reference 0 only for coarse 1-cycle matching when query length is severely limited, but treat its boundary values with caution. When query shows drift, match against reference 2 (upward drift) or 1 (downward drift) depending on slope sign; if query has elevated amplitude, compare to reference 3’s upper envelope.
uncertainties: Exact phase alignment tolerance (±3–5 points) not quantified visually
Whether very low-amplitude baseline wobble (<0.1) is intrinsic or measurement artifact
